title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: In (198) the 'def' labels appear to be swapped in the image. Under P(d,d')_{d'} Grothendieck writes something like P_d ⊗/×_{D_d} D_{d,d'}, and under P(d,d')_d he writes P_{d'} ×_{D_{d'}} D_{d,d'}. By analogy with (197), the correct definitions are P(d,d')_{d'} = P_{d'} ×_{D_{d'}} D_{d,d'} and P(d,d')_d = P_d ×_{D_d} D_{d,d'}. This is a harmless slip; the 'x' over the subscript is also overwritten.

Nothing else wrong. The claim 'épi lisse' is correct: the kernel of the projection torus T⊗G_m → T'⊗G_m is a torus, because the cokernel of the lattice map is free (in fact the map is split surjective).

ideas.what: Over each normal-crossings stratum D_d: a twisted rank-d lattice T_d (branch lattice), the torus G_d = T_d ⊗ G_m, and a G_d-torsor P_d of normal frames.
ideas.modern_name: Characteristic sheaf M̄^gp of the log structure of an snc/ncd pair and its associated torus torsor; the punctured normal bundle as a model of the deleted tubular neighbourhood (tangential base points).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Fontaine–Illusie and K. Kato (log structures, ~1988–89); Kato–Nakayama (1999).
ideas.where_published: Only hinted at in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), in the discussion of 'structure à l'infini' and tangential base points of Teichmüller towers.

ideas.what: Tautological projection of lattices Z^{I_d} → Z^J on the incidence variety D_{d,d'}, and the induced smooth surjection of tori.
ideas.modern_name: Generisation / cospecialisation map of the characteristic monoid (N^d → N^{d'}, face projection).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in log geometry and toroidal embeddings (Kempf–Knudsen–Mumford–Saint-Donat 1973; K. Kato).

ideas.what: Compatibility of normal-frame torsors under passage to a shallower stratum: P_{d'}|_{D_{d,d'}} ≅ P_d|_{D_{d,d'}} ∧^{G_d} G_{d'}.
ideas.modern_name: Pushout of torsors along a torus morphism; restriction of the normal bundle of a branch intersection to a deeper stratum.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (deformation to the normal cone of ncd strata).

ideas.what: Triple incidence D(d,d',d'') and the transitivity cocycle for lattices, tori and torsors.
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of the stratification / the log structure as a functor on the poset of strata (cone-complex / Artin-fan type data).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; in modern form Abramovich–Chen–Marcus–Wise (Artin fans), Ulirsch.

missed.claim: Grothendieck systematically organises the boundary of M̄_{g,ν} as a functor from chains d ≥ d' ≥ d'' to (lattice, torus, torsor) data. This is essentially the log/toroidal structure presented stratum-by-stratum, intended as input for the fundamental groupoids at infinity. The page itself is tautological set-up. The announced non-tautological relation (next page) may be of more interest, but it lies outside this page.
missed.quote: Toutes ces relations sont essentiellement tautologiques. En voici une qui ne l'est plus (next page)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents an independent, pre-log-geometry formalism for the 'structure à l'infini' used for anabelian purposes (tangential base points on M̄_{g,ν}). Its interest is historical rather than mathematical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but routine set-up of normal-crossings stratum data. This is now standard in log geometry (characteristic sheaves, torus torsors, cospecialisation maps). The only interest is historical: it shows Grothendieck building this framework independently for the structure at infinity of M_{g,ν}.

Struck passage reads approximately: 'On a des relations de transitivité [written above 'Au niveau des Groupoïdes fondamentaux'] pour les morphismes précédents, on peut dire que P(d,d')_{d'}'.
Following line likely: 'relativement [P(d,d')_d struck] à la donnée d'un triple d ≥ d' ≥ d''', then 'en se plaçant sur D(d,d',d''), on a [objets struck] systèmes locaux'.
